I notice some doc comments ended up AFTER `#[must_use]` attributes (e.g. lines 82-84, 101-103, 108-110). That's a problem: doc comments must come before attributes to attach to the item? Actually in Rust, doc comments are attributes themselves and order doesn't matter for whether they attach — both `#[must_use]` and `///` are outer attributes on the item. But wait, the doc comments inserted at line 83 come after `#[must_use]` at line 82, and both precede `pub fn system` at 84. That's fine — they all attach to the same item. Rust allows attributes in any order. Good.

All checks pass for my assigned files. Here's my result.

## Result

Documented the full client/transport/config/error surface (7 files, 230 doc lines added), in Portuguese, focused on implementer contracts:

- **`client/mod.rs`** — module docs for `http` and `token`.
- **`client/http.rs`** — `RawResponse` (fields + `validate`: `text/html`/`text/plain` always rejected, `xml` requires `xml`/`octet-stream` content-type, `%PDF`/`<?xml`/`<` magic bytes, `Content-Length` match). `MtrHttpClient` docs cover the **3-attempt retry** (1s/2s backoff) on 429/5xx/timeouts, **401 first-attempt refresh with async-mutex single-flight**, concurrency limit, and every public method.
- **`client/token.rs`** — `TokenManager`, refresh/integration tokens, **TTL clamping** (7-day cap, −60s skew, 8h fallback from JWT `exp`).
- **`transport/mod.rs`** — module docs with fully-qualified links, `HttpRequest`/`HttpResponse`, and the `HttpTransport: Send + Sync` **test seam** used by `build_with_transport`.
- **`transport/reqwest.rs`** — `ReqwestTransport::new` timeout/error contract.
- **`config.rs`** — `Config` fields, `builder` defaults, and `base_url` **validation/normalization** (http/https scheme, trailing-slash trim, defaults per system), `max_rps` zero rejection.
- **`error.rs`** — `ErrorKind` variants with status mapping, `OpenMTRError` RFC 7807 fields, all constructors, `http_error` status→kind table (401/404/422/Api), **`is_timeout`/`is_network`** semantics, and `error_types` URNs documented as **static `LazyLock`** values.

### Verification
- `cargo rustc ... -W missing_docs`: **none of my files** appear in the diagnostic list.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p open-mtr-core --no-deps`: **no errors/warnings point at my files**. No compilation errors from my changes; no stray edit markers.
- Fixed intra-doc links (used fully-qualified paths in `//!` module docs, dropped links to the private `MAX_TOKEN_TTL_SECS` and cfg-gated `ReqwestTransport`, replaced `r#type` with a plain literal).

One unrelated, pre-existing doc error remains outside my scope: `adapters/trait_def.rs:16` has an unresolved link to `crate::openmtr::OpenMtrClient` (owner: DomainDocs). It is the sole reason the overall `cargo doc` command still exits non-zero; my files are clean.
